text: A converging lens forms an inverted real image on the opposite side when the object lies beyond its focal point.
A converging lens forms an upright real image on the opposite side when the object lies beyond its focal point.
An object inside a converging lens's focal length produces an upright, magnified virtual image on the object's side.
An object inside a converging lens's focal length produces an upright, magnified virtual image on the lens's opposite side.
Parallel rays entering an ideal converging thin lens meet at its focal plane after refraction through the lens.
Parallel rays entering any real converging lens meet at one identical focal point regardless of their wavelength.
The thin-lens equation relates focal length to object and image distances measured from the lens's principal plane.
The thin-lens equation relates focal length to object and image distances measured from the lens's nearest surface.
Linear magnification equals image height divided by object height, with a negative sign convention indicating an inverted image.
Linear magnification equals image height divided by object height, with a positive sign convention indicating an inverted image.
For a real object, a diverging lens creates a reduced, upright virtual image between the lens and its focal point.
For a real object, a diverging lens creates a magnified, upright virtual image between the lens and its focal point.
As an object approaches a converging lens's focal point from beyond it, the real image recedes and becomes larger.
As an object approaches a converging lens's focal point from beyond it, the real image approaches and becomes larger.
Narrowing an ideal lens aperture dims the image and increases depth of field without changing the paraxial image position.
Narrowing an ideal lens aperture dims the image and increases depth of field by lengthening the lens's focal length.
Independent events satisfy the rule that learning one event occurred leaves the probability of the other event unchanged.
Independent events satisfy the rule that learning one event occurred raises the probability of the opposite outcome for the other.
After any recorded streak of heads from independent fair flips, the next coin flip still has one-half probability of heads.
After any recorded streak of heads from independent fair flips, the next coin flip has increased probability of tails.
Ten consecutive heads have probability one in 1,024, but after nine heads the conditional chance of another remains one-half.
Ten consecutive heads have probability one in 1,024, so after nine heads the conditional chance of another is one in 1,024.
Long sequences of independent random outcomes naturally contain clusters and streaks, even when every trial uses the same probability.
Long sequences of independent random outcomes should distribute evenly, so visible clusters and streaks indicate changing trial probabilities.
Independent events need not be mutually exclusive; their joint occurrence equals the product of their individual probabilities.
Independent events must be mutually exclusive; their joint occurrence equals the product of their individual probabilities.
For independent events, the probability that both occur equals the product of their individual probabilities.
For independent events, the probability that both occur equals the sum of their individual probabilities.
Independence describes the generating process, so an observed streak creates no balancing tendency in later trials.
Independence describes the generating process, so an observed streak creates a balancing tendency in later trials.
Stopping only after a desired streak biases the reported dataset, although it leaves each independent trial's probability unchanged.
Stopping only after a desired streak biases each trial's underlying probability, increasing the physical frequency of the selected streak.
A broad index fund reduces company-specific risk by holding many securities, but it remains exposed to overall market declines.
A broad index fund eliminates company-specific and market risk by holding enough securities across many industries.
Lower annual fund fees preserve more capital for compounding, so small fee differences substantially affect long-term wealth.
Lower annual fund fees affect only the first year's return, so small fee differences barely influence long-term wealth.
An index fund seeks to track a benchmark before costs, leaving actual investor returns slightly different because of fees and tracking error.
An index fund exactly matches its benchmark after costs, because passive management removes fees and tracking error.
Picking a few individual stocks concentrates both potential gains and company-specific losses compared with owning a broad market index.
Picking a few researched individual stocks preserves potential gains while diversifying company-specific losses as effectively as a broad index.
Diversification reduces risks unique to particular companies, but it cannot prevent losses caused by a broad market downturn.
Diversification reduces risks unique to particular companies and prevents losses caused by a broad market downturn.
Frequent stock trading creates transaction costs and taxable gains that reduce an investor's return in a taxable account.
Frequent stock trading defers taxable gains and reduces transaction costs, improving an investor's return in a taxable account.
A market-cap-weighted index assigns larger weights to companies with greater market values and changes those weights as prices move.
A market-cap-weighted index assigns equal weights to every company and preserves those weights as prices move.
Passive investing follows predefined rules rather than avoiding all trades; index funds rebalance when their benchmark composition changes.
Passive investing avoids all trades after purchase; index funds retain every original holding even when their benchmark composition changes.
An octave sounds strongly consonant because its frequencies form a two-to-one ratio, aligning many harmonics between both notes.
An octave sounds strongly consonant because its frequencies form a three-to-one ratio, aligning many harmonics between both notes.
A pure perfect fifth uses a three-to-two frequency ratio, causing numerous upper partials of its two notes to coincide.
A pure perfect fifth uses a four-to-three frequency ratio, causing numerous upper partials of its two notes to coincide.
Dissonant roughness increases when nearby partials fall within the same auditory critical band and produce rapid beating.
Dissonant roughness increases when nearby partials coincide exactly within the same auditory critical band and eliminate beating.
Perceived consonance reflects frequency relationships, tone spectra, tuning, musical context, and learned expectations rather than one universal ratio rule.
Perceived consonance reflects frequency relationships alone, because simple integer ratios determine chord quality regardless of timbre or musical context.
Equal temperament makes a perfect fifth slightly narrower than the pure three-to-two interval, supporting consistent transposition among keys.
Equal temperament makes a perfect fifth slightly wider than the pure three-to-two interval, supporting consistent transposition among keys.
Inverting a chord preserves its pitch classes but changes the bass note, spacing, acoustical spectrum, and perceived stability.
Inverting a chord preserves its pitch classes and therefore leaves the bass function, acoustical spectrum, and perceived stability unchanged.
A major triad combines intervals whose lower harmonics substantially overlap, helping many listeners hear the chord as fused and stable.
A major triad combines intervals whose fundamental frequencies exactly belong to one harmonic series in equal temperament, ensuring perfect stability.
A tritone creates tension through acoustical roughness and learned voice-leading expectations, with its effect depending on voicing and context.
A tritone always creates identical tension through acoustical roughness alone, with its effect independent of voicing and musical context.
Yeast makes bread rise by fermenting sugars into carbon dioxide, which expands inside bubbles supported by the dough's gluten network.
Yeast makes bread rise by fermenting sugars into carbon dioxide, which starch granules trap more effectively than the dough's gluten network.
Baking soda leavens dough efficiently when an acid supplies protons, allowing bicarbonate reactions to release carbon dioxide gas.
Baking soda leavens dough efficiently without an acid, because bicarbonate releases the same carbon dioxide immediately in plain water.
Baking powder contains both a base and dry acids, producing carbon dioxide after moisture and, for double-acting types, heat activate it.
Baking powder contains both a base and dry acids, producing carbon dioxide only after oven heat activates every type.
Kneading develops a connected gluten network that stretches around gas cells, helping dough retain fermentation gases as it rises.
Kneading develops a connected gluten network that generates carbon dioxide as its proteins cross-link, directly causing the dough to rise.
Overproofed dough collapses when its expanded gluten structure becomes too weak to retain gas during handling or baking.
Overproofed dough collapses when yeast exhausts available sugar and stops producing gas, despite the expanded gluten structure remaining strong.
Early oven spring comes from expanding gases, water vapor, and temporarily faster yeast activity before heat kills the yeast.
Early oven spring comes from expanding gases, water vapor, and sustained yeast fermentation that continues until the crust fully forms.
Moderate salt strengthens wheat dough and slows yeast fermentation, helping control both gas production and the final crumb structure.
Moderate salt weakens wheat dough and accelerates yeast fermentation, helping maximize gas production and the final crumb structure.
Sourdough rises through gases produced by its microbial community, while yeasts and lactic acid bacteria also create characteristic flavors and acidity.
Sourdough rises mainly through carbon dioxide from lactic acid bacteria, while yeasts create acidity and contribute little leavening gas.
Vaccines expose the immune system to selected antigens, expanding specific lymphocyte clones without requiring the full natural disease.
Vaccines expose the immune system to selected antibodies, expanding specific lymphocyte clones without requiring the full natural disease.
After vaccination, some activated B and T cells become long-lived memory cells that respond faster during later exposure.
After vaccination, all activated B and T cells remain permanently active, continuously producing a maximal response until later exposure.
Protective immunity involves pathogen-specific combinations of neutralizing antibodies, helper T cells, cytotoxic T cells, and memory responses.
Protective immunity depends exclusively on circulating antibodies, because T cells cannot recognize cells infected by pathogens.
A booster dose reactivates memory lymphocytes, increasing antibody quantity, binding affinity, and the durability of protection.
A booster dose replaces memory lymphocytes with naive cells, increasing antibody quantity, binding affinity, and protection durability.
Vaccine immunity develops over days or weeks because lymphocytes must activate, multiply, differentiate, and establish memory.
Vaccine immunity becomes complete within minutes because injected antigens immediately transform into long-lived antibodies and memory cells.
Messenger RNA vaccines deliver temporary cytoplasmic instructions for an antigen; the RNA is subsequently broken down without entering the nucleus.
Messenger RNA vaccines deliver permanent nuclear instructions for an antigen; the RNA integrates into chromosomes before cells express it.
Vaccine adjuvants stimulate innate danger signals that strengthen adaptive responses, but they do not supply pathogen-specific antibodies themselves.
Vaccine adjuvants supply pathogen-specific antibodies directly, eliminating the need for innate signaling during development of adaptive responses.
Widespread vaccination reduces pathogen transmission and indirectly protects vulnerable people without guaranteeing zero infections among vaccinated individuals.
Widespread vaccination indirectly protects vulnerable people only by curing their infections after transmission, rather than reducing transmission.
A B-tree index accelerates selective equality and range filters by locating relevant keys without scanning every table row.
A B-tree index guarantees constant-time equality and range filters by locating every relevant key with a single comparison.
Indexes speed many reads but add storage and write overhead because inserts, updates, and deletes also modify index structures.
Indexes speed many reads without affecting writes because inserts, updates, and deletes modify only the underlying table rows.
A composite B-tree index on columns A and B supports filtering by A because A is its leading column.
A composite B-tree index on columns A and B supports filtering by B equally well because column order is irrelevant.
A covering index contains every column needed by a query, permitting execution without extra row lookups in the base table.
A covering index contains every row in physical table order, permitting execution without filtering or sorting for any query.
For a filter matching most rows, a table scan costs less than repeated random row lookups through an index.
For a filter matching most rows, an index scan costs less because indexes remain faster at every selectivity.
Without a matching expression index, filtering on LOWER(name) prevents direct lookup through a conventional index on untransformed name values.
Without a matching expression index, filtering on LOWER(name) uses a conventional index that automatically derives transformed name values.
Stale statistics that misrepresent data distribution produce inaccurate cardinality estimates and steer the query planner toward inefficient execution plans.
Query planners derive exact row counts directly from SQL text, so stale table and index statistics cannot affect execution plans.
An index whose key order matches a query's ordering avoids a separate sort while scanning rows in index order.
Any index on the queried table avoids a separate sort, regardless of its indexed columns or key order.
Greenhouse gases warm the lower atmosphere by absorbing and re-emitting outgoing infrared radiation, slowing Earth's loss of energy to space.
Greenhouse gases warm the lower atmosphere mainly by reflecting incoming visible sunlight downward, increasing Earth's absorbed solar energy.
The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth's surface warmer than its airless radiative temperature, while added greenhouse gases enhance that warming.
The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth's surface cooler than its airless radiative temperature, while added greenhouse gases reverse that cooling.
Carbon dioxide accumulates when emissions exceed natural removals, so its warming influence depends strongly on cumulative human emissions.
Carbon dioxide cannot accumulate because natural sinks remove each year's emissions completely, so warming depends only on current annual emissions.
Water vapor mainly amplifies current global warming as a feedback because warmer air supports more atmospheric moisture.
Water vapor initiates current global warming as an independent forcing because extra atmospheric moisture raises temperature before any other change.
Increasing carbon dioxide tends to warm the surface and troposphere while cooling the stratosphere, a characteristic greenhouse-gas pattern.
Increasing carbon dioxide tends to warm the surface, troposphere, and stratosphere equally, a characteristic greenhouse-gas pattern.
The greenhouse effect raises the average altitude from which infrared escapes, where colder air emits less energy until temperatures adjust upward.
The greenhouse effect lowers the average altitude from which infrared escapes, where warmer air emits less energy until temperatures adjust upward.
A cold day describes local short-term weather and does not contradict a long-term rise in global average temperature.
A cold day directly contradicts a long-term rise in global average temperature because climate is the average of daily weather.
Methane produces stronger warming per emitted mass over short periods than carbon dioxide, but atmospheric methane is shorter-lived.
Methane produces weaker warming per emitted mass over short periods than carbon dioxide and remains in the atmosphere much longer.
Active pieces outweigh a small material deficit when immediate threats prevent the opponent from coordinating or consolidating.
Active pieces automatically outweigh any material deficit because immediate threats permanently prevent the opponent from coordinating or consolidating.
A rook on the seventh rank attacks pawns, restricts the enemy king, and creates threats worth more than passive material.
A rook on the seventh rank attacks pawns and restricts the enemy king, guaranteeing compensation for a sacrificed minor piece.
An initiative compensates for material only while forcing moves arrive quickly enough to deny the defender time for consolidation.
An initiative permanently compensates for material once forcing moves begin, even after the defender gains time for consolidation.
An exposed king makes extra material irrelevant when active enemy pieces coordinate a forced mating attack.
An exposed king remains safe when its side has extra material, because additional defenders neutralize every coordinated mating attack.
An advanced passed pawn compensates for sacrificed material when it ties down defenders and threatens promotion.
An advanced passed pawn compensates for sacrificed material whenever promotion remains legally possible, even without restricting any defender.
The bishop pair becomes especially active in open positions, where long diagonals allow both bishops to influence opposite-colored squares.
The bishop pair becomes especially active in closed positions, where blocked diagonals allow both bishops to influence opposite-colored squares.
A positional exchange sacrifice trades a rook for a minor piece to gain lasting activity, structure, or king pressure.
A positional exchange sacrifice trades a minor piece for a rook to gain lasting activity, structure, or king pressure.
Standard piece values are rough averages; mobility, coordination, pawn structure, king safety, and tactical timing determine practical value.
Standard piece values remain exact in every position; mobility, coordination, pawn structure, king safety, and timing cannot alter practical value.
Metals bend plastically when dislocations move through nondirectional metallic bonds without immediately separating the crystal.
Metals bend plastically when entire atomic planes separate through metallic bonds and then reconnect after deformation.
Ceramics shatter with little plastic deformation because strong directional or ionic bonds impede dislocation motion before fracture.
Ceramics shatter with little plastic deformation because strong directional or ionic bonds accelerate dislocation motion before fracture.
Microscopic flaws concentrate tensile stress in ceramics, driving rapid crack propagation once the local fracture threshold is reached.
Microscopic flaws distribute tensile stress throughout ceramics, allowing cracks to propagate rapidly once the average fracture threshold is reached.
Plastic deformation around a crack tip absorbs energy and blunts the crack, making many metals relatively tough.
Plastic deformation around a crack tip sharpens and accelerates the crack, making many metals relatively tough.
In susceptible metals, lower temperatures and faster loading suppress plastic deformation, producing more brittle fracture than warm, slow loading.
Lower temperatures and faster loading promote plastic deformation, making metals consistently more ductile than under warm, slow loading.
Within the Hall-Petch regime, reducing grain size strengthens a metal because grain boundaries hinder dislocation motion across neighboring crystals.
Within the Hall-Petch regime, increasing grain size strengthens a metal because fewer grain boundaries hinder dislocation motion across neighboring crystals.
Ceramics withstand compression better than tension because compression closes cracks while tension pulls crack faces apart.
Ceramics withstand tension better than compression because tension closes cracks while compression pulls crack faces apart.
Cold working raises dislocation density, making further slip harder and increasing metal strength while reducing ductility.
Cold working removes dislocations, making further slip harder and increasing metal strength while reducing ductility.
A p-value is the probability, assuming the null model, of obtaining results at least as extreme as those observed.
A p-value is the probability that the null hypothesis is true after obtaining results at least as extreme as those observed.
A small p-value measures incompatibility with the null model, not the size or practical importance of the observed effect.
A small p-value measures the size and practical importance of the observed effect, not merely incompatibility with the null model.
Rejecting a null hypothesis at a chosen threshold does not establish that the alternative explanation is practically important or causal.
Rejecting a null hypothesis at a chosen threshold establishes that the alternative explanation is practically important and causal.
Failing to reject the null means the data lack sufficient evidence against it, not that the null has been proven true.
Failing to reject the null means the data provide sufficient evidence that the null hypothesis has been proven true.
With a large sample, a scientifically trivial effect produces a very small p-value when estimation becomes sufficiently precise.
With a large sample, only a scientifically important effect produces a very small p-value because sample size removes trivial differences.
A p-value is trustworthy only to the extent that the sampling design, statistical model, and test assumptions are appropriate.
A p-value remains trustworthy even when sampling design and test assumptions fail because its calculation automatically corrects model errors.
Testing many hypotheses without adjustment increases the chance of finding at least one small p-value under true null hypotheses.
Testing many hypotheses without adjustment leaves the chance of finding a small p-value unchanged because every test is calculated separately.
For a matching two-sided test, a null value outside the corresponding confidence interval is rejected at the associated significance level.
For a matching two-sided test, a null value inside the corresponding confidence interval is rejected at the associated significance level.
Network latency measures how long data takes to travel, while bandwidth measures the data transferred per unit time.
Network latency measures the data transferred per unit time, while bandwidth measures how long each packet takes to travel.
A high-bandwidth connection still feels slow for interactive tasks when propagation, routing, or queueing produces high latency.
A high-bandwidth connection necessarily feels fast for interactive tasks because increasing capacity proportionally reduces propagation and routing latency.
Transferring a large file depends mainly on sustained throughput, while its startup also incurs latency from connection setup and requests.
Transferring a large file depends mainly on latency, while sustained throughput matters only during connection setup and requests.
Propagation delay comes from distance and signal speed, whereas transmission delay depends on packet size and link bandwidth.
Propagation delay depends on packet size and link bandwidth, whereas transmission delay comes from distance and signal speed.
A ping primarily estimates round-trip latency and packet loss; it does not directly measure a connection's available bandwidth.
A ping primarily estimates available bandwidth from round-trip latency, directly revealing the connection's maximum bulk transfer rate.
Video streaming needs enough sustained bandwidth, while online games depend more strongly on low and stable latency.
Video streaming depends mainly on low latency, while online games depend more strongly on maximum sustained bandwidth.
Congestion increases latency as packets wait in queues and reduces useful throughput through loss, retransmission, or contention.
Congestion increases bandwidth as packets accumulate in queues, improving useful throughput through retransmission and contention.
TCP throughput remains below link bandwidth when round-trip time, packet loss, or receive-window limits constrain data in flight.
TCP throughput always reaches link bandwidth regardless of round-trip time or packet loss because acknowledgments do not constrain data in flight.
